# Rupok

> Rupok is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) smartboard and whiteboard app for teachers. Teachers write on slides with fast GPU ink, drop in live interactive "Smart Objects" that an AI made (simulations, 3D models, quizzes), and replay every class stroke by stroke. It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop, with no install and no account. Students open lesson files (`.rpk`, RPK: Rich Presentation Kit) in the browser. Made by Shaitrish in Bangladesh.

Key facts (November 2026):

- Price: free, every feature. An optional hosted service, Rupok Cloud (sync, share links, live classes), is coming with a free plan.
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later for the app; the `.rpk` format spec, the reference reader/writer, the Smart Object SDK and the agent skills are Apache-2.0.
- Status: pre-alpha, actively developed. Open the app at https://rupok.app/board/
- AI: works with the AI you already use. Any chatbot can write a Smart Object as one HTML file to paste onto the board; Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode can build whole lessons through the `rupok mcp` server.
- Shipped: GPU ink, PDF slides, Smart Objects, stroke replay, Prepare/Teach/Student modes, the student viewer, Bangla text in lessons, the MCP server.
- Coming soon (not shipped): desktop app (Windows, Linux), offline install, Bangla interface, replay with audio, Rupok Cloud, a remote Claude connector, live classes.
- Logo: the logo is a rounded square cut on the diagonal, with the mint half slid away. Tagline: "Mind over matter".

## Use Rupok from an AI agent (MCP)

The `rupok` CLI includes an MCP server over stdio. The agent can only read and write lessons inside the workspace folder.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok && cd rupok
cargo install --path crates/rupok-cli                      # installs `rupok` (needs Rust)
claude mcp add rupok -- rupok mcp --workspace ~/Lessons    # Claude Code
```

- Codex CLI, `~/.codex/config.toml`: `[mcp_servers.rupok]` with `command = "rupok"` and `args = ["mcp", "--workspace", "/home/me/Lessons"]`
- OpenCode, `opencode.json`: `"mcp": { "rupok": { "type": "local", "command": ["rupok", "mcp", "--workspace", "/home/me/Lessons"] } }`
- Any MCP client: command `rupok`, args `mcp --workspace <dir>`, transport stdio.
- Tools: `list_lessons`, `create_lesson`, `get_lesson_outline`, `add_page`, `add_smart_object`, `update_smart_object`, `add_text`, `delete_item`, `set_page_background`, `validate_smart_object`, `read_object_spec`.
- Workflow: call `read_object_spec` once, plan one idea per page, write each object as self-contained HTML, then `validate_smart_object` and fix every error before `add_smart_object`.
- [Agent guide (skills/AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok/blob/main/skills/AGENTS.md): setup for every agent and the full tool reference
- [Smart Object skill](https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok/blob/main/skills/rupok-smart-objects/SKILL.md): how to write good Smart Objects

## Read a .rpk file (for AI models and agents)

A `.rpk` (Rich Presentation Kit) file is a Rupok lesson and a ZIP archive. Unzip it and read `content.md` first (the lesson as Markdown, page by page), or `content.json` (structured). Interactive Smart Objects are HTML in `objects/<id>/index.html`. The authoritative document is `doc.loro` (Loro CRDT; `pip install loro` or `npm install loro-crdt`).

- [RPK file format](https://rupok.app/rpk/): the human page ([Markdown twin](https://rupok.app/rpk.md))
- [Agent skill: read-rpk](https://rupok.app/skills/read-rpk.md): step-by-step instructions and the schema summary
- [read_rpk.py](https://rupok.app/skills/read_rpk.py): .rpk → Markdown with the Python standard library (uses `loro` when installed); [sample lesson](https://rupok.app/skills/sample-lesson.rpk)

## Comparisons (facts checked 23 Nov 2026, with sources)

- [Rupok vs Note3](https://rupok.app/compare/note3.md): Prestigio's paid, Windows-only EasiNote successor
- [Rupok vs SMART Notebook](https://rupok.app/compare/smart-notebook.md)
- [Rupok vs OpenBoard](https://rupok.app/compare/openboard.md): both free and open source
- [Jamboard alternative](https://rupok.app/compare/jamboard.md): Jamboard was discontinued on 31 Dec 2024
- [Rupok vs Microsoft Whiteboard](https://rupok.app/compare/microsoft-whiteboard.md): standalone apps retired 16 Oct 2026
- [Rupok vs ActivInspire](https://rupok.app/compare/activinspire.md)
- [Rupok vs Explain Everything](https://rupok.app/compare/explain-everything.md)
- [Rupok vs OneNote](https://rupok.app/compare/onenote.md)
